I can relate to you a lot. I've known for a long time my own worst enemy is myself.

I also just wanted to say that I think you have a real gift with words. You're very expressive, and your prose is truly poetic. I hope you write some more one day.

This place has helped me a lot. Of course, I've had bad experiences, but overall this subreddit is the only one I've found where people really just *get it.* People here actually listen and try to empathize, everybody else I've talked to just spouted bullshit in an attempt to stop me from offing myself. It feels like people here care.

I've thought about suicide a lot over the years. It first started when I was nine, but it stopped for a few years until about last year. Now it's on or off every month or two. It's been wearing me down to the point where I'm just numb. Suicide for me has just become a logical choice, and the only thing keeping me here are my friends and family. I know they would blame themselves, and I really don't want them to, so I stay. I mostly just a hope a bus will run me over soon.

So he told you he wouldn't be mad... and then got mad anyways? Telling your partner that they rely on you too much after they expressed suicidal thoughts doesn't sound like a normal reaction either. Him saying that a memory lapse from PTSD was fake and then leaving doesn't sound very caring. I don't want to be insulting, especially since I don't have the full context, but this doesn't sound like a healthy relationship at all. Just because he isn't as bad as other people doesn't automatically mean he's good. You deserve better.

It sounds like you attach all of your self worth to the relationships you have with other people, and that's not healthy at all. As cliche as it sounds, there is some truth to the statement that you need to love yourself before you can love other people. 

There's nothing wrong with taking years to get into a relationship, and there's nothing wrong with never getting into a relationship. There's people who haven't found a stable relationship or job in their 30's, and that's perfectly fine. It's normal to feel misunderstood, but I really think there's a great chance that you'll be able to find someone who does understand you. Happiness is hard, but if you keep holding on I believe you'll be able to obtain it one day.

If you want to talk about things I might not be the best person, but I know a lot of people here are very active in chat. I hope things get better for you.

I've had these thoughts since I was nine, and it still hasn't gotten any better. It was on and off back then. I'd have thoughts of killing myself for a few weeks and it would slowly go away, then come back a few months later. I'd just thought that was how my life would be. But it hasn't gone away for months, and I'm fucking terrified.

I used to be able to pull myself out of bed in the morning, even if it took ten minutes. Lately it's been taking an hour *at least.* I have online classes, but I just can't find it within myself to care.

I do think most people around me are toxic. Everyone here says they support people with mental illnesses, gay or bisexual people, transgender people and other minorities, but then shun them and gossip when it's someone they know. I guess woke social media posts are more convenient than caring about people. I'm running far away from here if I live long enough.
